problem: Mesh-based simulators (Habitat, iGibson, AI2-THOR) render with low photorealism, have costly asset authoring, and offer only low-fidelity mesh humanoids. Isaac Sim's 3DGS support is closed-source and needs RT-core GPUs.
motivation: Visual realism of simulated observations governs Sim-to-Real transfer, and agents must learn to navigate among dynamic humans. 3DGS gives cheap photorealistic assets from reconstructions or generative pipelines, but lacks explicit geometry for collision, so it needs integration into an open, Habitat-compatible pipeline.
key_idea: Extend Habitat-Sim with a zero-copy CUDA-OpenGL 3DGS renderer and drivable gaussian avatars (CUDA LBS), while decoupling visuals (3DGS) from navigation (NavMesh with dynamic proxy-capsule obstacles).
insight: Mixed mesh+GS training beats mesh-only or GS-only: mesh scenes give fast geometric learning, GS scenes give realism. Config E (20M+80G) reaches GS-test SR 79.6 vs 61.3 for mesh-only while keeping mesh-test SR on par, and mixed agents get the best real-video APA. GS-only converges slowly (mesh-test SR 53.0). Fine-tuning with gaussian avatars lowers CR/PSI on GS test, and the gains partly transfer to mesh avatar scenes.
method: 3DGS renderer: CUDA tile rasterizer writes color and depth into pre-registered OpenGL textures via zero-copy Map-Render-Unmap interop, so sensor outputs match the mesh format
Depth compositing: a full-screen shader keeps the nearer fragment between GS and mesh passes; all avatars are rasterized in one CUDA pass
Gaussian avatar module: canonical gaussians (from AnimatableGaussians) baked offline, deformed to SMPL-X poses by a CUDA LBS kernel with no runtime network inference
GAMMA trajectories: motion generated offline along NavMesh shortest paths, converted to per-frame SMPL-X joint matrices and interpolated at runtime
Dynamic NavMesh blocking: proxy capsules derived from SMPL-X bones are precomputed per frame and injected into the planner as dynamic obstacles, clipping colliding motion
Habitat-Lab APIs: nearest-avatar-capsule distance and step-blocked queries for reward shaping and metrics (CR, PSI); scene assets are imported as PLY from InteriorGS, self-reconstructions or Marble

setting.backbone: DD-PPO with ResNet visual encoder + GRU policy head (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: PointNav on 100 train scenes of HM3D mesh and/or InteriorGS+self-reconstructed GS scenes in varying mixtures, 5e7 steps; avatar fine-tuning 5e6 steps on 20 GS scenes with 3 gaussian avatars
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward, turn left/right, stop
setting.privileged: none beyond the standard PointNav goal vector (GPS+compass); NavMesh used for collision

numbers.extra: 5e7 training steps; cross-domain test with disjoint scenes
numbers.evidence: Table static_nav (a), GS Test, E: 20 M + 80 G

numbers.extra: static pretrain 5e7 + 5e6 fine-tune steps with 3 avatars

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks only, no standard-benchmark numbers. Sim-to-real APA±1 (self-recorded avg 61.2 for E, InCrowd-VI avg 29.6 for D) and performance FPS table are not in the metric format above.
results: Mixed-domain training (E: 20M+80G) raises GS-test SR to 79.6 from 61.3 for mesh-only (A) while keeping mesh-test SR at 59.6 vs 59.0. Mixed agents also get the best real-video APA±1. Gaussian-avatar fine-tuning cuts GS-test CR from 6.713 to 4.746 and PSI from 0.092 to 0.077. The simulator runs at 94 FPS with no avatars in a ~2M-Gaussian scene and 57.7 FPS with 2 avatars, versus 163.8 FPS for mesh.
limitations: Navigation-level collision only (NavMesh plus capsules); no physics-level interaction or manipulation of GS objects
Avatars follow pre-synthesized trajectories and are not reactive co-agents
Throughput drops versus mesh (about 51 FPS at 5M Gaussians; 24.7 FPS with 10 avatars), and the sim-to-real evaluation is open-loop on video only
